name: Corponation Loyalty Lanyard
description:
A neck lanyard in corponation-specific colors carrying an employee ID badge, access cards, and a small RFID token. Every corponation in GLMZ issues their own variant — Crucible's is copper and charcoal, Sentinel's is steel blue, Cascade's is white and green. The lanyard is technically just a badge holder. In practice, it is the most visible indicator of who you belong to.

Wearing your lanyard outside work hours signals that your identity and your employment are the same thing. Some employees never take them off. Some discard them the instant they leave the building. The choice says everything about the wearer's relationship with their employer.
functionality: Employee identification, access control, corponation affiliation display
what_it_says: You belong to a corponation and you either wear that identity proudly or haven't bothered to take it off yet.
story_hooks: A Crucible loyalty lanyard is found in a Sentinel Corp restricted area — either a defector, a spy, or someone who got very lost in a building they shouldn't have been in.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek neck lanyard worn suspended from shoulders, terminating at chest level with an integrated badge holder. The lanyard creates a vertical accent line down the torso, positioning corporate identity at the heart. Reads as both functional utility and psychological collar.
physical_description.fit: Adjustable length, worn loosely around neck to allow natural movement. Badge holder sits approximately 4-6 inches below collarbone. Not form-fitting; the lanyard itself is thin and minimal, letting the corponation colors dominate the visual impression.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade synthetic blend webbing with reinforced stitching. Material varies by corponation but maintains durability for daily handling—resistant to sweat, thermal fluctuation, and minor abrasion. Subtle sheen indicates technical treatment.
physical_description.texture: Smooth to slightly textured surface; the webbing has a tight weave that catches light subtly. Badge holder is hard composite plastic with precision-molded edges. RFID token adds discrete weight and a faint metallic finish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Corponation-specific: Crucible = copper and charcoal striped or blocked; Sentinel = cold steel blue with silver accents; Cascade = clean white with kelly green trim. Colors are unmistakable and intentionally bold for instant recognition.
physical_description.closures: Adjustable friction-fit clasp at back of neck or magnetic snap mechanism. Badge holder secured via tension clip or subtle velcro strips. No unnecessary ornamentation.
distinctive_features: Embedded RFID token adds subtle weight and defines corponation affiliation
Badge holder displays corporate logo and employee tier designation
Access card slots visible but secured
Stitching is precise and reinforced—signals investment in durability
Corponation colors are saturated and unmissable from distance
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 for employees who wear them; the lanyard itself indicates corporate employment. Wearing one outside work signals privilege, security clearance, and institutional identity.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is bound to a corponation. Wearing it off-hours signals either fierce loyalty, inability to separate self from work, or performative corporate dedication. Not wearing it when employed reads as quiet rebellion or compartmentalization of identity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and maintained if wearer takes pride in corporate affiliation; worn soft at edges and faded if constantly used; deliberately removed and stored if wearer maintains boundary between work and life.
